Q1Physics
subjectPhysics
streamnot applicable (Physics has no streams)
branchnot applicable (Physics has no branches)
chapterModern Physics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer depends on how the atomic number changes in alpha, beta-minus and beta-plus decay, which is covered under the Modern Physics topic 'Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Decay'.
subtopic 1Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Decay
subtopic 2not assigned (one subtopic chosen)
why this subtopicThe answer depends on how alpha, beta-plus and beta-minus emissions change the atomic number (Z-1, then Z-3, then Z-2).
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A radioactive nucleus AZX undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence AZX → Z-1B → Z-3C → Z-2D, Atomic number of element X. The possible decay particles in the sequence are:
  1. β+, α, β-
  2. β-, α, β+
  3. α, β-, β+
  4. α, β+, β-
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)
  1. AZX → AZ-1B - β+ Decay [atomic no. decreases by 1]
  2. Z-1B → Z-3C - α Decay [atomic no. decreases by 2]
  3. Z-3C → Z-2D - β- Decay [atomic no. increases by 1]

→ the working concludes: option 1

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · high
  1. In β+ decay Z → Z-1; in α decay Z → Z-2; in β- decay Z → Z+1.
  2. X → B: Δ Z = (Z-1) - Z = -1, so the particle is β+.
  3. B → C: Δ Z = (Z-3) - (Z-1) = -2, so the particle is α.
  4. C → D: Δ Z = (Z-2) - (Z-3) = +1, so the particle is β-.
  5. The sequence β+, α, β- is option 1.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
11 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsRecall the change in atomic number for α (-2), β-minus (+1) and β-plus (-1) decay → Read the atomic-number change at each stage of the sequence: Z to Z-1, Z-1 to Z-3, Z-3 to Z-2 → Map each change to its decay particle and match the ordered triple to an option
why it is trickyThe work is recalling the atomic-number change for each decay type and applying it to three successive transitions in order.
the catchOne option swaps beta-plus and beta-minus, which is exactly the result of confusing the sign of the charge change in beta decay.

The effective resistance of a parallel connection that consists of four wires of equal length, equal area of cross-section and same material is 0.25 Ω. What will be the effective resistance if they are connected in series?
  1. 1 Ω
  2. 4 Ω
  3. 0.25 Ω
  4. 0.5 Ω
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. Let each wire’s resistance be R
  2. When all 4 are in parallel:
  3. Req = R/4 = 0.25
  4. R = 1 Ω
  5. When all are connected in in series:

  7. = 4 Ω

  1. Four identical wires each of resistance R in parallel: Rp = R4.
  2. R4 = 0.25 Ω ⇒ R = 1 Ω.
  3. In series: Rs = 4R = 4 × 1 Ω = 4 Ω, which is option 2.

chapterCurrent Electricity high confidence
why this chapterThe answer depends on the relations for drift velocity, resistivity (rho = E/J), relaxation time and current density (J = n e v_d) for conduction in a metal, which current electricity teaches.
subtopic 1Resistivity
subtopic 2Drift Velocity
why subtopic 1The matches that separate the options are resistivity rho = E/J and relaxation time tau = m/(n e^2 rho), both from the microscopic expression for resistivity.
why subtopic 2The other half of the match depends on drift velocity, v_d = (eE/m)tau, and current density J = n e v_d, which are taught under drift velocity.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
Column-I gives certain physical terms associated with flow of current through a metallic conductor. Column-II gives some mathematical relations involving electrical quantities. Match Column-I and Column-II with appropriate relations.
ADrift VelocityPmne2ρ
BElectrical ResistivityQnevd
cRelaxation PeriodReEnτ
DCurrent DensitySEJ
  1. A-R, B-P, C-S, D-Q
  2. A-R, B-Q, C-S, D-P
  3. A-R, B-S, C-P, D-Q
  4. A-R, B-S, C-Q, D-P
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
  1. A-R, B-S, C-P, D-Q
  2. Direct Formula

→ the working concludes: option 3

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
  1. Drift velocity: vd = eEmτ, which matches R, so A-R.
  2. From J = σ E, resistivity ρ = 1σ = EJ, which is S, so B-S.
  3. σ = ne2τm = 1ρ gives τ = mne2ρ, which is P, so C-P.
  4. Current density J = nevd, which is Q, so D-Q.
  5. A-R, B-S, C-P, D-Q is option 3.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict

difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsRecall current density J = n e v_d to match D with Q → Recall Ohm's law in vector form E = ρ J, so resistivity = E/J, matching B with S → Rearrange ρ = m/(n e2 τ) to τ = m/(n e2 ρ) to match C with P (A-R is common to all options and needs no work)

subtopic 1Combination of Capacitors

why this subtopicThe answer 2C depends on reducing a mixed network: the middle capacitor is shorted by the connecting wire and the remaining two capacitors are in parallel, which is the combination-of-capacitors skill.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
The equivalent capacitance of the combination shown in the figure is:
  1. C/2
  2. 3C/2
  3. 3C
  4. 2C
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Ceq = 2C

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. Call the left terminal A and the right terminal B. The top capacitor joins A to node P, and the bottom capacitor joins A to node Q.
  2. Nodes P and Q both connect by plain wire to the right vertical wire, which is terminal B, so VP = VQ = VB.
  3. The middle capacitor sits between P and Q, so it has no potential difference across it. It is shorted and adds nothing.
  4. The top and bottom capacitors both lie between A and B, so they are in parallel: Ceq = C + C = 2C, which is option 4.

subtopic 1Newton's Law of Cooling and Bimetallic Strips
subtopic 2not assigned (one subtopic chosen)
why this subtopicThe answer (13/5 t) comes from applying Newton's law of cooling (average-temperature form) to the coffee cooling from 90 to 80 and from 80 to 60 degrees C in a 20 degree C room.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A cup of coffee cools from 900C to 800C in t minutes, when the room temperature is 200C. The time taken by a similar cup of coffee to cool from 800C to 600C at a room temperature same at 200C is
  1. 1013t
  2. 513t
  3. 1310t
  4. 135t
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Newton’s law of cooling:
  2. -Δ TΔ t = k[Tavg - T0]
  3. 1st case: 10°Ct = k[85 - 20]
  4. 2nd case: 20°Ct' k[80 + 602 - 20]
  5. 10t . t'20 = 6550
  6. t' = 13t5

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. Average-form Newton's law of cooling: Δ TΔ t = k(T - Ts).
  2. First cup: 90-80t = k(90+802 - 20) = 65k.
  3. So k = 1065t.
  4. Second cup: 80-60t' = k(80+602 - 20) = 50k.
  5. t' = 2050k = 20 × 65t50 × 10 = 135t, which is option 4.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
44 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsApply the averaged form of Newton's law of cooling to the first cooling: rate of fall (10 degrees per t) equals k times (mean temperature 85 minus 20) → Apply the same form to the second cooling: 20 degrees per t' equals k times (mean temperature 70 minus 20) → Divide the two equations to eliminate k and express t' as a multiple of t
why it is trickyThe work is two applications of the averaged Newton's law of cooling, one per interval, followed by taking their ratio to eliminate the cooling constant.
the catchOne distractor is the result of comparing only the excess temperatures (65/50) and ignoring that the second temperature drop is twice as large as the first.

why this chapterThe answer depends on the distance covered in the nth second under uniform acceleration from rest (Galileo's law of odd numbers, S_n proportional to 2n-1), which is kinematics; the smooth incline only sets a constant acceleration.
subtopic 1Galileo's Law of Odd Number
subtopic 2not assigned (one subtopic chosen)

printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time t = 0. Let Sn be the distance travelled by the block in the interval t = n - 1 to t = n, Then, the ratio SnSn + 1 is:
  1. 2n+12n-1
  2. 2n2n-1
  3. 2n-12n
  4. 2n-12n+1
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Snth = u + a2[2n - 1]
  2. u = 0
  3. a = gsinθ
  4. Snth = gsinθ2[2n - 1]
  5. S(n+1)th = gsinθ2[2n + 1]
  6. SnS(n+1) = 2n - 12n + 1

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. On a smooth incline the acceleration a = gsinθ is constant and the block starts from rest.
  2. Sn = 12a n2 - 12a(n-1)2 = a2(2n-1).
  3. Sn+1 = a2(2(n+1)-1) = a2(2n+1).
  4. SnSn+1 = 2n-12n+1, which is option 4.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict

stepsRecognise that on a smooth incline the acceleration a = g sin(θ) is constant and the block starts from rest → Apply the distance-in-nth-second relation S_n = (a/2)(2n-1), and likewise S_(n+1) = (a/2)(2n+1) → Take the ratio S_n / S_(n+1) so that a cancels

READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.

  2. [M1L2T-2] = [MLT-2]a[LT-2]b[Tc]
  3. M1L2T-2 = MaLa+bT-2-2b+c

Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. Energy is work done: E = F · L.
  2. Acceleration has dimensions [A] = [L T-2], so [L] = [A][T2].

  1. The field lines spread out to the right, so |→E| decreases with x: Eleft > Eright.

  3. From t = 4 to t = 6 s the ball falls for 2 s: vy = g t = 10 × 2 = 20 m/s.
  4. v = ux2 + vy2 = 202 + 202 = 202 m/s.
  5. The acceleration is g = 10 m/s2 downward, which is option 2.

Q50Physics

chapterRay Optics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer depends on using the lens formula to place the image formed by the convex lens, then reflection at the plane mirror to find the final image, which is ray optics.
subtopic 1Lens Formula
subtopic 2Reflection at a Smooth Surface
why subtopic 1The answer first requires the lens formula to place the lens image at 60 cm behind the lens (20 cm beyond the plane mirror), which then acts as a virtual object.
why subtopic 2The final answer (a virtual image 20 cm in front of the plane mirror) comes from reflection at the plane mirror, which forms the image of that virtual object at an equal distance on the other side, so the plane-mirror reflection step is a genuine second half of the solution.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A point object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a convex lens of focal length 30 cm. If a plane mirror were put perpendicular to the principal axis of the lens and at a distance of 40 cm from it, the final image would be formed at a distance of:
  1. 30cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image.
  2. 20 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image.
  3. 20 cm from the lens, it would be a real image.
  4. 30 cm from the lens, it would be a real image.
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. 1v - 1u = 1f
  2. 1v1 - 1(-60) = 130
  3. 1v1 = 130 - 160 = 160
  4. v1 = +60
  5. 1v2 - 1u = 1f
  6. 1v2 - 1(-20) = 130
  7. 1v2 = 130 - 120 = 1030 × 20
  8. v2 = -60

→ the working concludes: unclear

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. Sign convention (Cartesian, applied per surface): distances measured from the optical centre/pole, positive along the direction of the incident light at that element. Lens at x=0, object at x=-60 cm, mirror at x=+40 cm.
  2. First refraction at the lens (light travelling +x): u=-60, f=+30, so 1v=1f+1u=130-160=160, v=+60 cm.
  3. The converging rays heading for x=+60 meet the mirror at x=+40 first, so the lens image is a virtual object 60-40=20 cm behind the plane mirror.
  4. Reflection at the plane mirror: image is as far in front as the object is behind, so a real image forms 20 cm in front of the mirror, at x=+20 cm (rays converge there, then diverge travelling -x).
  5. Second refraction at the lens (light now travelling -x; take -x as positive): the point at x=+20 is a real object on the incoming side, u=-20, f=+30.
  6. 1v=130-120=-160, so v=-60 cm: the image is on the incoming side, 60 cm from the lens at x=+60.
  7. Light then leaves the system travelling -x and does not meet the mirror again; the final image is virtual (rays diverge from x=+60).
  8. Final image: virtual, 60 cm from the lens, i.e. 60-40=20 cm from (behind) the plane mirror, which matches option 2.
